extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Nature Progress and Communications journals (Nature Portfolio)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers evaluating manuscripts submitted to Nature Progress and Communications journals, covering publication criteria, how to write reviews, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, timing, transparent peer review, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: The conclusions are novel
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusions are novel (we do not consider abstracts and online preprints to compromise novelty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is judged by the reviewer; abstracts and online preprints do not compromise novelty for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong evidence for main conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper provides strong evidence for the main conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the data and analyses convincingly support the principal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art data generation and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying data are generated and processed at a state-of-the-art level, including tracking of uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess data quality, processing pipelines, error/uncertainty quantification and whether methods represent current best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance in understanding in line with journal aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript represent an advance in understanding in line with the journal aims and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the manuscript's contribution to the journal’s stated aims and scope (see the relevant journal page for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the editors with the information needed to reach a decision and instruct the authors on how they can strengthen their paper to the point where it may be acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out arguments for and against publication; provide editors with the evidence and reasoning on which they should base a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the major claims of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the major claims of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the principal claims so editors and authors understand what the manuscript asserts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty and prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims novel? If not, please identify the major papers that compromise novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If novelty is compromised, cite specific prior work and explain how it affects the manuscript's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the paper be of interest to others in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the potential readership and relevance of the findings to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence on thinking in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the paper influence thinking in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the findings are likely to change approaches, hypotheses, or future research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincingness of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims convincing? If not, what further evidence is needed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify missing controls, analyses, or data that would be required to make the claims convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend additional experiments or analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there other experiments that would strengthen the paper further? How much would they improve it, and how difficult are they likely to be?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between essential work required for publication and optional extensions; estimate effort and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate discussion in context of literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims appropriately discussed in the context of previous literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether authors have cited and fairly interpreted relevant prior work and situate their contribution correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission potential
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript is unacceptable in its present form, does the study seem sufficiently promising that the authors should be encouraged to consider a resubmission in the future?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise whether the work could reach publishable standard after major revisions or additional experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript clearly written? If not, how could it be made more accessible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unclear sections, suggest restructuring or language edits to improve communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the manuscript be shortened to aid communication of the most important findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend deletions or compressions that would sharpen the paper’s message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding overselling
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors done themselves justice without overselling their claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for exaggerated language or claims that exceed the evidence and advise moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair treatment of previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Have they been fair in their treatment of previous literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note omissions or biased representation of prior studies and request corrections or additional citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient methodological detail for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Have they provided sufficient methodological detail that the experiments could be reproduced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request source code, detailed protocols, mathematical derivations, or other materials required for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the statistical analysis of the data sound?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate appropriateness of tests, handling of multiple comparisons, sample sizes, error reporting and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting further data or methods for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the authors be asked to provide further data or methodological information to help others replicate their work? (Such data might include source code for modelling studies, detailed protocols or mathematical derivations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify exactly what additional material should be made available and whether it is essential or optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns with animals or human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any special ethical concerns arising from the use of animals or human subjects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag ethical issues, inadequate approvals, or omissions in reporting relevant to subjects or animal welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the review process as strictly confidential and not discuss the manuscript with anyone not directly involved in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to consult laboratory colleagues (identify them to editors). Check with editors before consulting experts outside your institution to avoid involving excluded individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly (normally within two weeks of receiving a manuscript) and notify the editor if a longer delay is anticipated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews support rapid editorial decisions; if delayed, inform the journal so alternative reviewers can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and signing reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identities are not released to authors or other referees unless reviewers specifically sign their comments to authors; signing is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer reports, whether signed or not, are shared with other reviewers. Reviewers who prefer anonymity should avoid seeking confirmation of identities; the journal will neither confirm nor deny speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing of reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not suppress reviewers reports; on rare occasions we may edit a report to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should avoid language that may cause needless offence; main points intended for authors will generally be transmitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest—when to decline
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reviewing when you have conflicts: authors have excluded you; recent or ongoing collaborations; commented on drafts; in direct competition; history of dispute; financial or any other interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, draw the editor’s attention to anything that might affect your objectivity. Conflicts are not always clear-cut; experts closest to the field may still be appropriate reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection is based on many factors including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and previous experience of a reviewer’s characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may avoid requesting reviews from people who do not return reviews timely or do not provide reasoning for their views (whether harsh or lenient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments to the authors and author rebuttal letters may be published online as a supplementary peer review file; by agreeing to review you give consent to potential publication of reviewer comments made to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential reviewer comments to the editor or other correspondence will not be published. Reviewer names will only be published if the reviewer signed their comments or explicitly agrees to release their name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online manuscript review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should submit their comments via the online submission system using the link provided in the editor’s email; uploading attachments is discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal email for help with the system if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to literature support
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer does not have access to any published paper necessary for evaluation, the journal will supply the reviewer with a copy on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the publication reference to the editor who sent you the paper; the editor will obtain and forward it (paying any necessary fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers' accountability and AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are accountable for the accuracy and views expressed in their reports. Do not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools; if any part of your evaluation was supported by an AI tool, declare the use transparently in the peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the journal's AI policy and transparently report any AI assistance used in your evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to re-review revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When referees agree to review a paper, this is a commitment to review subsequent revisions as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will not send resubmitted papers back to reviewers if it seems the authors have not made a serious attempt to address the reviewers' criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting and use of reviewer recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are welcome to recommend a particular course of action but editors make the final decision and will weigh the arguments rather than count votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasoned arguments for and against publication; editors evaluate the strength of arguments as well as other information not available to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reviewer disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may consult other reviewers or bring in additional reviewers when referees disagree or a dispute arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be willing to provide follow-up advice if requested, though editors try to limit prolonged disputes and consultation to what is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting technical criticisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal takes reviewers' technical criticisms very seriously and is reluctant to disregard them; if one reviewer alone opposes publication, editors may consult others about whether an unduly critical standard is being applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, technically grounded criticism; editors may seek to resolve apparent unfairness or overly harsh standards by consulting additional reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to referees after decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked to re-review a revised manuscript, reviewers normally receive copies of other reviewers' comments; the journal routinely informs reviewers of decisions and sends copies of other reviewers' reports by email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are normally informed when a paper is accepted despite their negative recommendation; being overruled does not imply lack of confidence in a reviewer's judgment.
